keyVerseText: When the waves of death compassed me, the floods of ungodly men made me afraid; waves: or, pangs ungodly: Heb. Belial
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun מִשְׁבָּר (mishbâr) derives from the root שָׁבַר (shâbar), which fundamentally means to break or burst, whether literally or figuratively. This root conveys the sense of something that is violently broken or crushed, suggesting sudden, forceful disruption. Thus, mishbâr as a noun captures the essence of a breaker or a breaking wave, emphasizing the dynamic and powerful motion of the sea that shatters or rends.
usageInScripture: Mishbâr appears five times in Scripture, consistently referring to the physical phenomenon of waves or breakers of the sea. Translations such as "When the waves," "all thy waves," and "me about all thy billows" reflect its use in describing the overwhelming and tumultuous forces of water. This consistency in usage highlights the word's vivid portrayal of natural power, often employed figuratively to symbolize calamities or divine judgment sent by God.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding mishbâr enriches our grasp of biblical imagery where the sea’s breakers symbolize overwhelming trials and divine wrath. The word’s root meaning of breaking underscores the intensity and disruptive nature of these waves, reminding believers of the reality of spiritual and earthly challenges that can threaten to overwhelm. Yet, recognizing that these breakers are under God's sovereign control invites faith in His power to sustain and deliver. Christ’s lordship over the chaos of life is echoed in this imagery, encouraging trust amid turmoil.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 22:5, the psalmist declares, "When the waves of death compassed me, the floods of ungodly men made me afraid," using mishbâr to evoke the crushing and relentless force of death and hostile enemies. The word intensifies the sense of being surrounded and overwhelmed, illustrating the psalmist’s peril. This vivid metaphor deepens our understanding of divine deliverance, as the broken waves represent not only physical danger but also spiritual assault from the wicked.
